title: Assessing Culture and the Governance of Conduct
summary: How supervisors assess firm culture through its drivers and observable behaviours, and how boards and senior managers govern conduct risk and are held accountable for it.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How supervisors assess firm culture through its drivers and observable behaviours, and how boards and senior managers govern conduct risk and are held accountable for it.
Learning Objectives: Explain the drivers of culture and why supervisors assess them
Assess board oversight, management information and accountability for conduct
Gather and triangulate evidence on culture from multiple sources
Syllabus: Drivers of culture: purpose, leadership, people, governance and incentives
Board oversight of conduct and senior manager accountability regimes
Evidence of culture: interviews, focus groups, surveys and documents
Red flags: tone at the top versus behaviour in the middle
Intended Audience: Conduct and consumer protection supervisors, including those supervising retail-facing firms
Prudential and governance supervisors seeking to assess culture and its link to risk
Policy, data and enforcement staff working on conduct risk and customer outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of conduct or consumer protection supervision is helpful. No background in economics or behavioural science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
